blurb: Graduate mathematical logic: completeness, compactness, computability, incompleteness, NP-completeness and ZFC.

pics.alt: Black-and-white portrait of the young Kurt Gödel in round glasses, suit and tie
pics.caption: Kurt Gödel as a student in Vienna, 1925. His 1929 dissertation proved the completeness theorem for first-order logic, and in 1931 he published the incompleteness theorems.
pics.title: Young Kurt Gödel as a student in 1925.jpg

pics.alt: Printed page of symbolic logic showing proposition 54.43 of Principia Mathematica and its proof
pics.caption: Proposition ∗54.43 of Whitehead and Russell's Principia Mathematica (volume I, 1910): the union of two disjoint unit classes has two members. The authors remark that 1 + 1 = 2 will follow from it once arithmetical addition has been defined.
pics.title: Principia Mathematica 54-43.png
pics.artist: Alfred North Whitehead and Bertrand Russell
